note: The world's NPC registry. WHICH type uses which movement, how many of them, how fast and WHERE THEY MAY STAND is data; the movements themselves stay code, because they are physics. Edited by the world editor (source id npc-types) and read by src/game/npcs.js.

movements.rail: walks a road's arclength at a fixed acera offset, crossing now and then (advancePed)
movements.bounded-random: random walk contained by an area, turning back at its edge (advanceFieldPed / advanceSwimmer)
movements.route: follows an authored polyline (advanceEditorRoute), or a bus (advancePassenger)

hostVocabulary: A hosts entry is either a SURFACE class name from src/game/surfaces.js (water, land, beach, road, paseo, bridge, acera, boulevard) or a host reference kind:use (parcel:pool, parcel:stadium, cuadra, landmark). The surface entries are checked against the raster; the host entries against properties.host.

types.name: Peatón
types.note: The city's ambient crowd. Rail-bound to a road so it can never wander into a cuadra interior.

types.name: Aficionado
types.note: The crowd on a cancha. gap is enforced twice — at spawn and every frame — because two random walks on one pitch meet. inset keeps it off the acera band the renderer paints over the block edge.

types.name: Bañista
types.note: radius is the body clearance from the kerb: testing the centre alone let them ride half-on the balneario's inner acera.

types.name: Pasajero
types.note: The one TEMPORARY kind: joinTheSidewalk drops both the flag and the type when an alighting passenger reaches the acera, so a person who got off a bus simply IS a person walking.

types.name: Pescador
types.note: He is seated in HIS BOAT'S frame, not standing on a surface: the estero's pangas draw him inside their own transform so he leans and bobs with the hull. That is why his host is water — the ground under him is the panga, and the only thing the world can check is that she is floating.

types.name: Pescador de muelle
types.note: People used to fish off the Muelle de Cruceros and do not any more; this is that, kept. He STANDS on the deck (host `bridge` — class 5 is the pier), unlike `fisher`, who is seated in a boat, so he carries the side of the muelle he is leaning over: the caña has to go out over the water, and which way that is depends on which edge he picked.
